sections: From Semantic Graphs to Executable Language

semantic_memory.title: Semantic Memory
semantic_memory.gap: They do not specify operations or obligations.

semantic_web.title: Semantic Web
semantic_web.strength: Shared identifiers and linked statements support knowledge exchange.

ontologies.title: Ontologies
ontologies.gap: An ontology alone does not order computation.

rdf.title: Rdf
rdf.strength: A standard graph data model supports exchange and traversal.
rdf.gap: It does not provide an instruction language.

owl.title: Owl
owl.strength: Ontology logic enables inference over semantic statements.
owl.gap: Inference and general operations remain distinct.

petri_nets.title: Petri Nets
petri_nets.strength: Transition firing makes a graph computational.
petri_nets.gap: Operations do not carry the semantic vocabulary of knowledge graphs.

parallel_graphs.title: Parallel Graphs
parallel_graphs.strength: Graph models support reasoning about parallel computation.
parallel_graphs.gap: They do not provide controlled English or obligations.

dataflow.title: Dataflow
dataflow.strength: The graph directly defines the flow of computation.
dataflow.gap: Operations remain opaque to a shared semantic vocabulary.

actors.title: Actors
actors.strength: Message-passing agents provide a graph model of computation.
actors.gap: Message content is not a closed semantic language.

statecharts.title: Statecharts
statecharts.strength: A visual graph can be readable and executable.
statecharts.gap: It does not provide the semantic graph language described here.

tensorflow.title: Tensorflow
tensorflow.gap: Operation meanings are supplied separately from the graph.

spark.title: Spark
spark.strength: Distributed dataflow graphs support large computations.
spark.gap: The graph does not type the meaning of its instructions as controlled English.

controlled_languages.title: Controlled Languages
controlled_languages.strength: Controlled languages demonstrate precise constrained natural language.
controlled_languages.gap: The surveyed tradition commonly targets logic rather than a mutable general graph.

ace.title: Ace
ace.strength: Constrained English can represent knowledge unambiguously and support OWL translation.
ace.gap: The cited approach targets logic rather than a general graph of operations.

attempto.title: Attempto
attempto.strength: English specifications produce queryable Prolog for simulation and validation.
attempto.gap: The Prolog is not decompiled back to the authored sentence.

cpl.title: Cpl
cpl.strength: Restricted English supports acquiring and using knowledge.
cpl.gap: Its knowledge target is not the typed general graph used here.

peng.title: Peng
peng.strength: English can serve as a formal specification surface.
peng.gap: The paper places it in the logic-targeted language tradition.

formal_semantics.title: Formal Semantics
formal_semantics.strength: Compositional semantics links language to precise formal meaning.
formal_semantics.gap: Logical representations are not directly the operational graph.

sydney_owl.title: Sydney Owl
sydney_owl.strength: Controlled language maps bidirectionally to OWL.
sydney_owl.gap: The target is ontology logic rather than a general graph of computation.

answer_sets.title: Answer Sets
answer_sets.strength: Programs can be specified and verbalised with semantic round trips.
answer_sets.gap: The target is a logic program and the round trip is semantic rather than token-preserving.

owl_services.title: Owl Services
owl_services.strength: Semantic descriptions support discovery, invocation and composition of services.
owl_services.gap: There is no controlled-language sentence surface or sentence decompilation.

opm.title: Opm
opm.strength: One diagram integrates structure and behavior and supports executable simulation.
opm.gap: Text is generated from diagrams; the vocabulary lacks obligation and permission modalities.

opcat.title: Opcat
opcat.strength: A bimodal tool supports object-process models.
opcat.gap: The diagram is authored first; it lacks typed deontic edges.

exekg.title: Exekg
exekg.strength: Semantic machine-learning pipelines translate into executable Python.
exekg.gap: The GUI-authored approach is specific to analytics and carries no obligations.

model_extraction.title: Model Extraction
model_extraction.strength: Language models help build graphs from unstructured sources.
model_extraction.gap: Extraction stages can lose information and require schema and knowledge fusion.

models_and_graphs.title: Models And Graphs
models_and_graphs.strength: Models and knowledge graphs can complement each other.
models_and_graphs.gap: Extraction does not itself eliminate the representation gap.

json_ld.title: Json Ld
json_ld.strength: A standard linked-data representation supports precise exchange.
json_ld.gap: Direct authoring still commonly needs translation tools.

property_graphs.title: Property Graphs
property_graphs.strength: Properties and relations support flexible graph storage.
property_graphs.gap: The storage model is not a constrained English surface.

mcp.title: Mcp
mcp.strength: A protocol standardizes tool requests and responses.
mcp.gap: Communication mechanics do not establish shared word meanings.

langgraph.title: Langgraph
langgraph.gap: Node content remains code or opaque natural language.

autogen.title: Autogen
autogen.gap: The topology does not type the meaning of their content.

crewai.title: Crewai
crewai.gap: The hierarchy does not define a closed semantic language for instructions.

dspy.title: Dspy
dspy.strength: Typed signatures and declarative modules give pipelines semantic structure.
dspy.gap: Semantics are at module granularity rather than every instruction word.

guided_generation.title: Guided Generation
guided_generation.strength: Constrained decoding enforces structured output syntax.
guided_generation.gap: Valid structure alone does not ensure valid meaning.

slot.title: Slot
slot.strength: Structured generation improves output format compliance.
slot.gap: Format compliance alone does not validate semantic combinations.

trugs.title: TRUGS
trugs.strength: Controlled English compiles to a typed general graph with a syntactic round trip and typed obligations.
trugs.gap: It requires a closed vocabulary and valid compositions; extraction from arbitrary prose still needs a separate process. This sample uses core relations, is unsigned, and does not implement the draft hub services.
